A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Unlasting and contain complete, readable main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–C. Text comparison and visual inspection support reliable matching throughout.

before.justification: v1 reports original perturbation-prediction experiments on Adamson, sci-Plex3 and Norman in Tables 1–2, plus ablations in Figure 6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and ablations, revises genetic-perturbation scores and adds ScLambda results.

M1.justification: The DDIB framework, conditional diffusion and GRN components, masked training objective, DDIM generation and Appendix A mask model are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Adamson single-gene knockouts, sci-Plex3 drug/dose prediction and unseen drugs, and Norman double-gene perturbations. No dataset, population or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds ScLambda to the Adamson comparison across all six metric/gene-subset combinations. Existing comparators remain, and comparator membership in the other comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported preprocessing, splits, gene counts, metrics, training budgets and sampling settings are identical. No revised protocol is documented for the replaced scores or the added ScLambda comparison.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and Figure 6 retain identical ablations of control statistics, latent initialization, masking and GRN information. Figure 5's gene-expression distribution analysis is also unchanged.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same score-plus-± reporting practice. Although many numerical quantities change, neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 substantially revise genetic-perturbation results. Adamson all-gene E-distance changes from 1.4442 to 0.8426 for Unlasting and 3.7594 to 0.8705 for GRAPE; Norman's corresponding values change from 1.2040/3.1600 to 0.7040/0.7722, markedly narrowing reported margins. Six ScLambda results are added. Chemical-perturbation results and Figure 6 remain unchanged. These are reported-score revisions without a documented method or protocol change.

T1.justification: The diffusion, GRN, masking and generation equations, along with the metric definitions in Appendix B, are identical. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about unpaired prediction, GRN guidance, silent-gene masking, distribution-aware evaluation and superior performance. The revised results do not change these claims' wording or scope.

C2.justification: The DDIB-as-augmentation explanation and interpretations of comparative results and ablations are unchanged. No new limitations or qualifications address the revised performance margins or added comparator.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, hyperparameters, preprocessing instructions and A100 hardware information remain identical, including Appendices A and C. No comparator implementation details or code/data access information are added.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and 31-entry bibliography are unchanged. ScLambda appears only as an added table row, without a corresponding citation or research-positioning discussion.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v1 dated 26 June 2025 to v2 dated 13 August 2025. Prose, terminology, headings, section order and appendix wording otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a ScLambda row. Table 2 moves from page 8 to page 9, shifting Figure 6 and subsequent text. Figures themselves, table columns and captions remain unchanged; the conclusion and references reflow.

improvement.justification: ScLambda adds a useful comparison, but the extensive score revisions are not reconciled with Figure 6, which retains the earlier Adamson values. Table 1 also continues highlighting Unlasting's DE20 EMD of 0.0950 despite ScLambda's lower 0.0904. The additional comparison and these unresolved reporting inconsistencies leave the net effect on paper quality uncertain.
